newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa falls back after approaching highs.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa falls back after approaching highs.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa made early advances on Tuesday but shed most of its gains after trade selling and profit-taking in New York, traders said.
The market approached recent highs in morning trade but was just short of resistance levels and then fell back in the afternoon as New York eased.
Traders said there was a lot of origin selling in London as well as some long liquidation.
"London shed its gains after trade selling and speculative profit-taking in the States," a trader said.
"Everybody's really looking at the stock market at the moment rather than commodities," he said.
Active December closed three stg up at 1,053 after touching 1,068, one stg short of its recent high of 1,069, in the morning session.
Benchmark September ended four stg up at 1,024 after reaching 1,037 -- 17 stg up -- in the morning session and then falling back.
Volume was 7,723 lots, well up on recent trading levels. December led with 2,703 lots followed by September with 1,837.
The back months rose three to seven stg.
On the fundamental side, light rain fell in southern Ivorian cocoa areas this week, favouring the 1997/98 crop prospects after a dry start to August.

Crop analysts said occasional light rains into September should confirm a large main crop from October despite the possibility of dry weather later this year from El Nino weather patterns already affecting other parts of the world.
The International Cocoa Organisation (ICCO) announced that it would meet with weather experts on September 10 to discuss the effects of El Nino on cocoa producing countries.
